title: Google Will Now Tell You If an Ad Was Made With AI
hook: Wondering whether that Google or YouTube ad is AI-generated? There's now a real answer, sitting in a settings menu most people have never opened.
key_points: Google added a 'created or edited with AI' label, visible in My Ad Center's 'how this ad was made' tab.
It covers ads on Google Search, Google Discover, and YouTube.
The labeling relies on Google's own disclosure system, applied at the ad platform level.
It's a practical tool: a real setting you can actually go check, not just a policy statement.
content_html: As AI-made images and video get harder to spot by eye, transparency tools are shifting from "trust us" statements to actual settings you can check. The Verge reports Google added exactly that: a "created or edited with AI" label, visible under the "how this ad was made" tab in My Ad Center, covering ads across Google Search, Google Discover, and YouTube.
extra_html: The value here isn't flashy, but it's real: instead of guessing whether a striking ad was AI-made, there's now a specific place to check. It joins a small but growing category of concrete AI-disclosure tools — alongside things like library apps letting readers filter AI-narrated audiobooks — that put a checkable fact in front of users rather than a general assurance. As with any self-disclosed labeling system, its usefulness depends on how consistently Google applies it across the ads running through its platforms. But knowing the setting exists at all is the first step; most people will never benefit from a transparency tool they don't know is there.

related.title: Your Library App Is Adding an AI Content Filter — Sort Of
related.hook: Libby, the library ebook app, is letting readers hide AI-generated books, narration, and art. The catch: the filter only works if publishers and authors honestly disclose using AI.

related.title: Spotting AI-Made Content
related.hook: There are real tells for AI text and images — but they're fading fast, and 'AI detector' tools are unreliable. The durable skill is judging the source, not squinting at the pixels.

flashcards.prompt: Where can you actually check whether a Google or YouTube ad was made with AI?

choices.text: The 'how this ad was made' tab in Google's My Ad Center
There's no way to check — it's not disclosed anywhere
Only Google employees can see this information

flashcards.explanation_html: Google added a specific, checkable label in My Ad Center rather than just a general policy — it's a concrete tool, not just a promise.

flashcards.prompt: What kinds of ads does this new label cover?
flashcards.back_html: Ads on Google Search, Google Discover, and YouTube — anywhere Google shows ads across its own major surfaces.
